note: The bands the SIG Kadet Senior plant has to land in, from docs/KADET-STAGE1.md, which derives each from SIG's published figures, O.S.'s for the FS-52 Surpass, an owner's measured rpm on its 12 x 6 and the drawn model (scripts/kadet-derive.js prints the derived figures). Each band is the Bombshell's in proportion about its derived figure, which is the Slow Stick's, unless its source says otherwise. Never widened to pass; argue in the derivation instead.

s1_level_75.source: level speed at 75 percent of the throttle stick, which is 81 percent of the engine's rpm, derived 14.58: the cruise SIG trims the Kadet at, 'with the model flying at about 3/4 throttle, feed in down trim until the model flies level'

s2_stall.source: sqrt(2W / rho S CLmax), derived 7.15; alphaStall is CLmax / CLalpha, 1.15 / 5.029, of the zero lift line

s4_top.source: level speed at full throttle, derived 18.28

s5_climb.source: full throttle, best over a sweep of airspeeds the plant flies unstalled, derived 4.92 at 10.1 m/s

s6_self_level.source: from a 30 deg bank at cruise, every stick centred: the four state lateral model gives 25.7, 22.5 and 19.7 deg after 2, 4 and 6 s, a spiral that halves the bank in 10.6 s; the bank at 6 s, the same side, and never steeper than it started

s7_rudder_bank.source: full right roll stick, which is full right rudder, from level cruise: 20.3 deg after 1 s by the lateral model, right wing down

s8_turn.source: a level 45 deg bank held on the rudder at full throttle: the radius against V^2 / (g tan bank) at the bank and speed flown, the Cub's 15 percent, and the radius itself against the 33.2 m the level turn flies at 18.1 m/s with 1.8 deg of up elevator, within the same 15 percent

s9_stall_power_off.source: full up from level flight at 1.2 Vs, 8.58 m/s, throttle closed, held 16 s (the Bombshell's 8 s scaled by the two phugoids, 10.1 s against 5.6) and read over the last 2 s: the pitching moment, taken back through the stall (the post stall model of docs/STALL-STAGE1.md), trims at 13.6 deg of alpha and the aircraft settles into a mush at 9.0 m/s sinking 1.88 m/s, within 25 percent; no wing drop, no yaw that is a spin, the nose never plunging

s9_stall_power_on.source: the same with the throttle opened to half, where the 12 x 6 at 9 m/s pulls 4.3 N against the mush's 5.6 N of drag: no wing drop, no spin, no plunge. Not the Bombshell's cruise throttle, where the FS-52 pulls 9.8 N, climbs the Kadet at full up and hangs it on its prop, which is not a stall

s10_phugoid.source: the phugoid root of the four state longitudinal model trimmed at the 14.58 m/s cruise, derived 10.06

s11_prop_torque.source: static full throttle, rolling left: ideal disc power 0.349, the 12 x 6's shaft power at a power coefficient of 0.045 0.579; the Bombshell's band about the two

s12_chop.source: throttle to idle from cruise, pitch stick neutral: a glide, not a tumble

s13_throw.source: the manual's hand launch: 'run into the wind at a fast trot and thrust the model forward with the nose slightly up in a spear throwing motion. It is not necessary to achieve a lot of velocity ... The model may dip slightly and then should begin to climb at a slight angle'. Thrown at 9 m/s, 1.26 Vs, 5 deg nose up at full throttle, the elevator where it trims level flight at 9 m/s (kadet:derive, the hand launch: 6.90 deg, stick 0.592) and every other stick centred: after 3 s it has not dipped the 1.5 m from the hand to its wheels touching, and it is over 1.2 Vs

s14_rest.source: the drawn model at rest, level, the CG 0.3072 m up; with the engine idling its 1.63 N held back by the wheels at the ground and its thrust line's moment lean it onto the nose wheel, 28.7 percent of the weight and 0.34 deg nose down (kadet:derive, at rest idling), within half a degree and 5 mm

s15_takeoff.source: full throttle on grass from standing, the elevator eased up from 1.1 Vs as the manual's 'a lot of elevator application is required for liftoff': it lifts off between 1.1 and 1.5 Vs, and between the rolls to those speeds at the rest attitude, 4.42 and 9.63 m (kadet:derive)

s16_landing.source: a glide from 8 m at idle, flown down at 1.3 V_s, 9.3 m/s, on the elevator and flared from 1.2 m: touches under the Bombshell's margin over the stall, 1.23 V_s, and comes to rest on its three wheels at S14's attitude, no hull or prop

s17_unmoved.source: the five inch's canonical replay hash and every other aircraft's recorded flight hash in Node, all from main's module at 512f915, before the Kadet existed The fixed wings' hashes were re-recorded on 2026-09-27 when their packs and tanks began to drain, the owner's decision (docs/POWER-STAGE1.md); the five inch's is unchanged.

s18_cross_host.source: the Kadet's recorded take off and flight, state trace hash, Node against headless Chrome

s20_idle.source: the throttle closed on the strip: the carburettor idles the FS-52 at O.S.'s lowest practical 2,300 rpm, 24.2 percent of the 9,500 it turns the 12 x 6 at, within 5 percent, and its 1.63 N of static thrust is under the 2.14 N of the wheels' rolling resistance, so the engine turns and the wheels' friction holds the aircraft: its ground speed is nil

s21_hands_off_glide.source: level at cruise, then the throttle closed and every stick let go, in Manual: the idle's thrust is nil over its 5.8 m/s pitch speed and the neutral elevator's pitching moment trims the glide at 3.3 deg of alpha, CL 0.292, 14.1 m/s sinking 2.32 m/s (kadet:derive, hands off glide). The mean of 5 to 15 s, after the phugoid's first cycle; the sink band is S3's in proportion, the speed band S1's, and it never reaches the stall's alpha
